title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 6 — Science | Food Sources
description: Subject-wise test on Food Sources (Science) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 6. 40Q.
subject: maha6-science

questions.question: What is the primary source of food for all living organisms, either directly or indirectly?

options.explanation: Animals are not the primary source of food for all living organisms.
Water is essential for life but is not a source of food.
Plants are the primary source of food for all living organisms.
Minerals are not the primary source of food for all living organisms.

questions.explanation: Plants are producers; they make their own food using sunlight and are the base of almost all food chains, providing food directly or indirectly to all other living organisms.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following food items is an animal product?

options.explanation: Rice is a plant product.
Spinach is a plant product.
Honey is an animal product produced by bees.
Wheat is a plant product.

questions.explanation: Honey is produced by bees, which are animals. Rice, spinach, and wheat are all plant products.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: An animal that eats only plants or plant products is called a:

options.explanation: Carnivores eat only animal products.
Herbivores eat only plant products.
Omnivores eat both plant and animal products.
Scavengers eat dead animals.

questions.explanation: Herbivores are animals whose diet consists exclusively of plant material.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: When we eat potatoes, which part of the plant are we consuming?

options.explanation: Potatoes are not roots.
Potatoes are modified stems.
Potatoes are not leaves.
Potatoes are not flowers.

questions.explanation: Potatoes are modified stems (tubers) that store food. While they grow underground, they are botanically considered stems, not roots.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of these is a common source of cooking oil derived from plants?

options.explanation: Milk is an animal product.
Egg is an animal product.
Groundnut is a plant product used for cooking oil.
Meat is an animal product.

questions.explanation: Groundnut (peanut) is a common oilseed from which cooking oil is extracted. Milk, egg, and meat are animal products.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Assertion (A): Humans are classified as omnivores. Reason (R): Humans consume both plant-based foods and animal-based foods.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation for A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation for A.
options.explanation: The reason does explain the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Humans eat a variety of foods, including fruits, vegetables, grains (plant-based) and meat, milk, eggs (animal-based). This characteristic of eating both plants and animals defines an omnivore, so the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: If you are eating a radish, what part of the plant are you consuming?

options.explanation: Radishes are not stems.
Radishes are not leaves.
Radishes are roots.
Radishes are not fruits.

questions.explanation: Radishes are root vegetables, meaning the edible part is the swollen taproot of the plant.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following food items is NOT obtained from an animal?

options.explanation: Cheese is obtained from animals.
Curd is obtained from animals.
Sugar is obtained from plants.
Ghee is obtained from animals.

questions.explanation: Cheese, curd, and ghee are all dairy products made from milk, which comes from animals. Sugar is primarily obtained from plants like sugarcane or sugar beet.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: A deer feeds on grass, and a tiger hunts the deer for food. Based on this observation, what can we infer about the deer and the tiger's food sources?

options.text: The deer is a carnivore, and the tiger is a herbivore.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct answer.

options.text: Both the deer and the tiger are herbivores.
options.explanation: The tiger is not a herbivore.

options.text: The deer is a herbivore, and the tiger is a carnivore.
options.explanation: The deer eats plants, and the tiger eats animals.

options.text: Both the deer and the tiger are omnivores.
options.explanation: There is no indication that either the deer or the tiger eat both plants and animals.

questions.explanation: The deer eats grass (a plant), making it a herbivore. The tiger eats the deer (an animal), making it a carnivore.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which plant part is commonly consumed as a food source in the form of beans or pulses?

options.explanation: Roots are not typically eaten as beans or pulses.
Stems are not typically eaten as beans or pulses.
Leaves are not typically eaten as beans or pulses.
Beans and pulses are the seeds of plants.

questions.explanation: Beans and pulses (like lentils, chickpeas) are the seeds of various plants, which are rich in protein and a common food source.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following food items is primarily obtained from a plant source?

options.explanation: Milk is obtained from animals
Eggs are obtained from animals
Wheat is a plant product
Honey is obtained from animals

questions.explanation: Wheat is a grain that grows on plants. Milk, eggs, and honey are products obtained from animals.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Animals that eat only plants or plant products are known as:

options.explanation: Carnivores eat meat
Herbivores eat plant-based food
Omnivores eat both plants and animals
Scavengers eat dead animals

questions.explanation: Herbivores are animals whose primary food source is plant-based. Carnivores eat meat, and omnivores eat both plants and animals.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which part of the spinach plant do we commonly eat as a vegetable?

options.explanation: Root is not the part of spinach we eat
Stem is not the part of spinach we eat
Leaf is the part of spinach we eat
Flower is not the part of spinach we eat

questions.explanation: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, and its leaves are the part consumed.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of these food products is obtained from animals?

options.explanation: Rice is a plant product
Potato is a plant product
Paneer is an animal product
Mango is a plant product

questions.explanation: Paneer is a cheese product made from milk, which comes from animals like cows or buffaloes. Rice, potato, and mango are plant products.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Identify the odd one out based on its food source:

options.explanation: Chicken is an animal product
Fish is an animal product
Cabbage is a plant product
Mutton is an animal product

questions.explanation: Cabbage is a plant product. Chicken, fish, and mutton are all animal products (meat).
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Why do humans and other living things need food?

options.explanation: Sleep is not the primary reason for needing food

options.text: To get energy for daily activities
options.explanation: Food provides energy for daily activities
Feeling sad is not related to needing food
Becoming lazy is not related to needing food

questions.explanation: Food provides the necessary energy for all life processes, including growth, repair, and performing daily activities.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Assertion (A): A tiger is a carnivore. Reason (R): A tiger eats grass and plants. Choose the correct option:

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason R is false

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Assertion A is true, but Reason R is false

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion A is true, and Reason R is false

options.text: Both A and R are false.
options.explanation: Assertion A is true, but Reason R is false

questions.explanation: A tiger is indeed a carnivore (eats meat), so Assertion A is true. However, tigers do not eat grass and plants; they eat other animals, so Reason R is false.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an omnivore?

options.explanation: Cow is a herbivore
Lion is a carnivore
Bear is an omnivore
Deer is a herbivore

questions.explanation: Bears consume both plant matter (like berries and roots) and animal matter (like fish or small mammals), classifying them as omnivores. Cows and deer are herbivores, and lions are carnivores.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Imagine a forest where most of the deer population suddenly disappears due to a disease. What is the most likely immediate impact on the tiger population in that forest?

options.explanation: Tiger population will not increase due to decrease in deer population

options.text: The tiger population will remain unchanged.
options.explanation: Tiger population will be affected due to decrease in deer population
Tiger population will decrease due to decrease in deer population

options.text: The tiger will start eating only plants.
options.explanation: Tigers are carnivores and will not start eating plants

questions.explanation: Deer are a primary food source for tigers. If the deer population decreases, tigers will have less food, leading to a decrease in their population due to starvation or reduced reproduction. Tigers are carnivores and will not start eating plants.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: A dish contains ingredients like flour, sugar, and butter. Which of these ingredients comes from an animal source?

options.explanation: Flour is a plant product
Sugar is a plant product
Butter is an animal product
Only butter is an animal product

questions.explanation: Flour comes from grains (plants), and sugar comes from sugarcane or sugar beets (plants). Butter is made from milk, which is an animal product.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is primarily a plant-based food source?

options.explanation: Eggs are animal products.
Milk is an animal product.
Rice is a grain obtained directly from the rice plant, making it a plant-based food source.
Honey is an animal product produced by honeybees.

questions.explanation: Rice is a grain obtained directly from the rice plant, making it a plant-based food source.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Animals that consume only plant parts as their food are categorized as:

options.explanation: Herbivores are animals whose diet consists exclusively of plant material.
Carnivores are animals that eat other animals.
Omnivores are animals that eat both plants and animals.
Scavengers are animals that eat carrion or dead animals.

questions.explanation: Herbivores are animals whose diet consists exclusively of plant material, such as grass, leaves, or fruits.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which part of the potato plant is commonly eaten as food?

options.explanation: Leaves of the potato plant are not commonly eaten.
Flowers of the potato plant are not commonly eaten.
Fruits of the potato plant are not commonly eaten.
A potato is an underground stem (tuber) of the potato plant, which stores food and is consumed by humans.

questions.explanation: A potato is an underground stem (tuber) of the potato plant, which stores food and is consumed by humans.

questions.question: Which of these food items is a product obtained from animals?

options.explanation: Spinach is a plant-derived food.
Ghee is clarified butter, which is made from milk, an animal product.
Wheat is a plant-derived food.
Mango is a plant-derived food.

questions.explanation: Ghee is clarified butter, which is made from milk, an animal product.

questions.question: Honey is a sweet substance produced by honeybees. This makes honey an example of a food product obtained from:

options.explanation: Honey is not obtained from plants.
Honeybees are insects (animals) that produce honey, making it an animal-derived food product.
Honey is not obtained from fungi.
Honey is not obtained from minerals.

questions.explanation: Honeybees are insects (animals) that produce honey, making it an animal-derived food product.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Identify the animal that has a different food habit compared to the others:

options.explanation: Lions are carnivores.
Tigers are carnivores.
Cows are herbivores, unlike the other animals listed.
Wolves are carnivores.

questions.explanation: Lions, Tigers, and Wolves are carnivores as they eat other animals. A Cow is a herbivore as it eats only plants.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following ingredients commonly used in cooking is obtained from both plant and animal sources?

options.explanation: Salt is a mineral, not obtained from plants or animals.
Water is not obtained from plants or animals in the context of cooking ingredients.
Some oils are plant-based, while others are derived from animals.
Sugar is typically plant-derived (sugarcane/sugar beet).

questions.explanation: While most cooking oils are plant-based (e.g., sunflower, groundnut), some oils like fish oil (cod liver oil) or animal fats (lard) are derived from animals.

questions.question: A person prepares a meal using lentils, rice, and a vegetable curry. All the main ingredients in this meal are primarily sourced from:

options.explanation: The main ingredients are not animal-derived.
Lentils, rice, and vegetables are all plant-derived.
The main ingredients are not minerals.
The main ingredients are not fungi.

questions.explanation: Lentils (pulses), rice (grain), and vegetables are all derived from plants.

questions.question: In a small garden, a gardener notices caterpillars eating the leaves of his tomato plants. He then observes birds feeding on these caterpillars. Considering this scenario, what are the feeding classifications for the tomato plant, the caterpillar, and the bird, respectively?

options.explanation: The classifications do not match the scenario.
The tomato plant is a producer, the caterpillar is a herbivore, and the bird is a carnivore.
The classifications do not match the scenario.
The classifications do not match the scenario.

questions.explanation: The tomato plant produces its own food (Producer). The caterpillar eats the plant (Herbivore). The bird eats the caterpillar (Carnivore).

Eggs are obtained from animals.

Cows are herbivores and primarily eat plants, not meat.
Humans are omnivores and consume both plants and animals.

questions.question: Which plant part are we referring to if it's a Potato?

A potato is not a flower.

questions.question: Which plant part are tomatoes, cucumbers, and bell peppers?

options.explanation: Roots are underground plant parts, but tomatoes, cucumbers, and bell peppers are not roots.
Stems are above-ground plant parts that provide support, but tomatoes, cucumbers, and bell peppers are not stems.
Leaves are the green, flat parts of plants that make food, but tomatoes, cucumbers, and bell peppers are not leaves.
Tomatoes, cucumbers, and bell peppers are botanically classified as fruits because they develop from the ovary of a flower and contain seeds.

questions.explanation: Tomatoes, cucumbers, and bell peppers are botanically classified as fruits.
